closed_lost_detail.business_issue_details: MIT Consulting is a Canadian MSP that has already decided to leave ConnectWise after roughly seven years and is looking for a PSA that can support the whole business, not just service desk. They need a modern, integrated platform for ticketing, projects, CPQ/quoting, opportunities, account management, invoicing, payments, agreements, distributor purchasing, reporting, and telecom billing consolidation. Their current stack is fragmented across ConnectWise, legacy CPQ, BrightGauge, Benji Pay, NinjaOne documentation/assets, Acronis, QuickBooks Online, and DataGate/telecom billing. The decision is
closed_lost_detail.problems_identified:
- ConnectWise has not scaled with the business, and the team is month-to-month while actively seeking a replacement.
- Current workflow spans too many systems: PSA, CPQ, reporting, payments, RMM/docs, backup, QBO, and telecom billing.
- The older ConnectWise CPQ experience creates gaps around quoting, templates, distributor pricing, optional items, approvals, and quote-to-project handoff.
- Cost/margin visibility on quotes is a major open concern; they need to see cost, margin, and distributor cost inputs during quoting.
- Accounting and billing depth are critical; Halo was viewed as weak on invoicing, and MIT needs confidence around QBO, agreements, recurring billing, block hours, project billing, payments, and consolidated invoices.
- Onboarding quality and contract flexibility are sensitive due to negative ConnectWise/Kaseya experiences.
- Canadian data residency, QBO Canada behavior, and telecom billing integration need clear confirmation.

Good persona for a client, but we don't have a Kaseya VSA integration and ConnectWise does. They know they need to switch off on prem VSA before switching PSA's, since no one else integrates. It's just such a large undertaking that they would need to tackle first as they can't do both migrations at the same time. A reason was required above so selected co-managed since we discussed that as well, but not a dealbreaker.

No dedicated PSA; customer data scattered across SharePoint/OneDrive
Manual recurring agreement management via SharePoint/email, no system of record
No parent-child account structure for billing roll-up or related accounts
Ticketing with no formal intake, boards, or status tracking
No mobile/field tooling (dispatch, GPS, mobile ticket access)
Hesitancy to onboard a new software due to bad previous experiences onboarding other platforms

rows.business_issue: Single Points of Failure across employee resources
rows.business_issue_details: Computer Speak / R-Options is evaluating Rev.io PSA as part of a broader modernization effort for a field-service / integrator business that is currently paper-heavy and dependent on QuickBooks for accounting and Salesforce as a contact manager. The company needs a system that can support day-to-day operations across quoting, proposal creation, ticketing, dispatch, purchasing, inventory, billing, tax, and reporting without disrupting accounting continuity. Their biggest concern is preserving QuickBooks financial reporting while improving operational control, especially around QuickBooks sync
rows.problems_identified:
- Existing workflows are manual and paper-heavy, creating friction for technicians, office staff, and leadership.
- QuickBooks is central to accounting, so any new system must preserve financial reports, P&L visibility, classes, item categories, and invoice/payment accuracy.
- Inventory and purchasing are operational pain points, especially for bill-as-quoted work where actual materials can differ from quoted quantities.
- The team needs confidence that ticketing, dispatch, project management, analytics, and security permissions will support real day-to-day usage.
- Vendor insurance certificate tracking is unresolved; current QuickBooks alerts flag expired certificates during PO creation.
- Adoption risk is meaningful because this is a major process change for a business with limited modern software experience.

rows.business_issue_details: Canitan is re-evaluating Rev.io after previously signing up during early access but not completing the transition due to platform gaps at the time, especially project management and QuickBooks sync. They are now comparing Rev.io against Field Motion 2.0 and need to decide soon, ideally by end of week and definitely within two weeks. Their main focus is whether Rev.io can now support their workflows, field technicians, project billing, inventory/assets, reporting, and customer-specific processes.
rows.problems_identified: Canitan’s current system / Field Motion option is less expensive and would require fewer changes, but it does not appear to offer the same depth Rev.io now has around mobile, project management, billing, reporting, inventory, asset tracking, automation, and AI. They also have workflow-specific needs around custom forms, multi-step job processes, asset tagging/scanning, customer coverage visibility, project billing across many tickets, multiple clock-ins per day, and technician permissions. Switching systems is a concern because of retraining, process recalibration, and cost.

rows.next_step: Follow-up Demo pending. Calling 8/21 at 4pm est if no response from meeting recap email
rows.business_issue: Digital Transformation
rows.business_issue_details: Technology West Group is evaluating Rev.io as a modern platform to centralize sales, service, project management, dispatch, mobile tech workflows, quoting, and billing. They are a Las Vegas AV integrator serving large casino customers, with complex project and invoicing needs. Richard is the current champion/evaluator, with Brandon and Natalie needing to be included in the next broader demo. Target decision timeline is end of year.
rows.problems_identified: Technology West currently manages project work through Google Sheets, while service/ticketing is handled mainly through email. They previously tried Freshdesk but abandoned it, and prior PM tools failed due to adoption issues. Sales uses DTools for CRM/quoting, ADP is used for time tracking, and QuickBooks Desktop is used for accounting. Their large casino customers often have highly customized invoicing requirements, and some projects may require AIA/retainage billing, which is a known Rev.io gap today.

rows.business_issue: Single Points of Failure across employee resources
rows.business_issue_details: Grey Matter MSP is evaluating whether to replace Halo PSA because the platform was implemented without intentional workflow design and is not supporting how the business actually operates across MSP/help desk, physical security, and audio-visual project work. They need a PSA that connects procurement, project management, assets, field mobility, reporting, and billing so revenue is captured accurately and teams can work from one operational system.
rows.problems_identified:
- Halo does not flow cleanly from purchase order/sales order into project execution, budgets, assets, and cost tracking.
- Field technicians lack a strong mobile workflow, causing notes and time to be entered in bulk later, which creates missed detail and inaccurate time capture.
- Help desk and project work live in separate operational “worlds,” with limited cross-visibility and no unified calendar view.
- Static billing misses dynamic changes like license count increases, overtime, and project time.
- Reporting is weak enough that they rely on CloudRadial for client-facing reporting and previously used BrightGauge internally.
- Procurement notifications and received-item workflows are not intuitive.

David is the primary technical evaluator, with Tim/Mr. King, Keith, and Mr. Benford needing involvement as the evaluation progresses.

ConnectWise Sell is viewed as expensive for limited value, permissions/RBAC are not controlled well enough, quote approvals are a concern, and the mobile app has syncing issues that create billing review work. The legacy on-prem codebase also makes AI harder to apply effectively.⁠
